notes.summary: Structural A and normalization are proved: Lee curvature is real, closed, exact and of type (1,1), with the stated conformal covariance. Smooth semipositive representatives give positivity against every Gauduchon test.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves the local primitive identities, positivity of Q, conformal covariance, and integration by parts for the ordinary Bott–Chern pairing. A’s nontriviality is deferred to n3. Neither Gauduchon existence nor Lamari sufficiency is used.
notes.text:
Use d^c=i(barpartial−partial)/(4π), dd^c=i partial barpartial/(2π), and ordinary wedge powers without factorial division. Write α=λ^{1,0}. Since λ is real, λ=α+conjugate(α), and
Q=λ∧λ^c=i α∧conjugate(α)/(2π).
Thus Q is real semipositive of type (1,1), with rank one wherever λ≠0.

Here is a direct local primitive argument. On a small real coordinate ball centered at 0, write λ=sum a_j(x)dx_j and define f(x)=integral_0^1 sum a_j(tx)x_j dt. Closedness gives partial_k a_j=partial_j a_k. Differentiation therefore gives partial_k f=integral_0^1 [a_k(tx)+t sum x_j partial_j a_k(tx)]dt=a_k(x). Hence λ=df locally, λ^c=d^c f, and κ=−dd^c f locally. The displayed dd^c normalization follows from barpartial partial=−partial barpartial. For real f, dd^c f is real and of type (1,1). Consequently κ is globally real, closed and of type (1,1). It is de Rham exact with global primitive −λ^c. This does not establish Bott–Chern triviality.

For global smooth real a, differentiation gives d(e^aω)=(λ+da)∧e^aω. The new closed Lee form is λ'=λ+da, with [λ']=[λ]≠0, and κ'=−d(λ^c+d^c a)=κ−dd^c a. Thus the ordinary real Bott–Chern class—closed smooth real (1,1)-forms modulo dd^c of global smooth real functions—is conformally invariant. Its nontriviality is proved in n3.

For any smooth real u and smooth (n−1,n−1)-form Γ, Stokes twice gives integral_X dd^c u∧Γ=integral_X u dd^cΓ. Indeed, integrating d(d^c u∧Γ) first gives integral dd^c u∧Γ=integral d^c u∧dΓ. Integrating d^c(u dΓ) makes the latter integral equal to −integral u d^c dΓ=integral u dd^cΓ. The integral of a d^c derivative of degree 2n−1 is zero: its relevant partial and barpartial terms are d derivatives after selecting their types, so ordinary Stokes applies.

Therefore, for EVERY positive Hermitian γ satisfying dd^c(γ^{n−1})=0, a smooth representative K=κ+dd^c u satisfies integral κ∧γ^{n−1}=integral K∧γ^{n−1}. If K≥0, this pairing is nonnegative. If K is nonzero, it is strictly positive: pointwise K∧γ^{n−1}=(trace_γ K)γ^n/n, and the trace is positive on a nonempty open set. A smooth closed semipositive K is itself a closed positive current. A global smooth u is genuinely quasi-plurisubharmonic: on every relatively compact coordinate ball its Levi form is bounded below, so adding a sufficiently large multiple of |z|^2 makes it plurisubharmonic.

Only differentiation, Hermitian linear algebra and Stokes are used. Artifact: proofs/n1.txt, serialized with notes.json by python build_notes.py. This proves structural A and the smooth every-test pairing fact, without asserting unrestricted pseudoeffectivity.

notes.summary: B is proved in every dimension by Stokes, including all mixed integrals and the strictly increasing actual volume polynomial. No Gauduchon hypothesis is needed.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves integral κ^kω^{n−k}=(n−k) integral Qκ^{k−1}ω^{n−k}, the positive first integral, and zero top integral. The actual V(t)=integral(ω+tκ)^n has degree at most n−1 and derivative n(n−1) integral Qω(ω+tκ)^{n−2}>0 wherever the ray is positive. These particular integrals do not provide all Gauduchon tests.
notes.text:
By n1, dκ=0. The LCK equation gives d(ω^m)=mλ∧ω^m for every nonnegative integer m. For 1≤k≤n, the graded Leibniz rule gives
 d(λ^c∧κ^{k−1}∧ω^{n−k})
 =−κ^k∧ω^{n−k}+(n−k)Q∧κ^{k−1}∧ω^{n−k},
because dλ^c=−κ and λ^c∧λ=−Q. This is the derivative of a global form of degree 2n−1. Stokes therefore proves exactly
 integral_X κ^k∧ω^{n−k}=(n−k) integral_X Q∧κ^{k−1}∧ω^{n−k}.
For k=n this gives integral κ^n=0. For k=1, Q∧ω^{n−1} is nonnegative and strictly positive wherever λ≠0. Nonexact λ cannot vanish identically, so smoothness gives such a nonempty open set. Since n≥2, integral κ∧ω^{n−1}=(n−1) integral Q∧ω^{n−1}>0.

Set η_t=ω+tκ and V(t)=integral_X η_t^n, using ordinary powers. Its binomial expansion is the actual integral polynomial. The coefficient of t^n is integral κ^n=0, so its degree is at most n−1. Crucially dη_t=dω=λ∧ω. Thus
 V'(t)=n integral_X κ∧η_t^{n−1},
 d(λ^c∧η_t^{n−1})=−κ∧η_t^{n−1}+(n−1)Q∧ω∧η_t^{n−2}.
Stokes yields
 V'(t)=n(n−1) integral_X Q∧ω∧η_t^{n−2}.
Whenever η_t is positive, this integrand is nonnegative and strictly positive where λ≠0. Pointwise, choose an η_t-unitary coframe placing the rank-one Q in the first direction. The restriction of ω to the remaining n−1 directions has positive trace; wedging with η_t^{n−2} gives a positive multiple of that trace. This also covers n=2, when η_t^0=1. Hence V'(t)>0 wherever η_t>0.

No dd^c(ω^{n−1}) or dd^c(η_t^{n−1}) condition was imposed. These identities do not establish positivity against EVERY Gauduchon test. Artifact: proofs/n2.txt; rerun python build_notes.py. These are ordinary all-dimensional proofs.

notes.summary: A is completed: the ordinary Bott–Chern Lee-curvature class is nonzero on every compact strictly LCK manifold, despite being de Rham exact.
notes.detailedSummary: A globally dd^c-exact curvature could be killed by a conformal rescaling. Applying B to the resulting strictly LCK metric contradicts its positive first curvature integral. This avoids any identification of de Rham and Bott–Chern cohomology.
notes.text:
Suppose {κ}=0 in ordinary real Bott–Chern cohomology. By definition, κ=dd^c a for a global smooth real a. If the quotient is initially expressed using complex functions, taking real parts provides such a real a because κ is real.

Set ω'=e^aω. By n1 this is smooth positive LCK, its closed Lee form λ'=λ+da remains nonexact, and κ'=κ−dd^c a=0. Apply n2’s k=1 identity to these actual rescaled tensors:
 integral_X κ'∧(ω')^{n−1}=(n−1) integral_X λ'∧(λ')^c∧(ω')^{n−1}>0.
The inequality follows from [λ']≠0 and n≥2, exactly as proved in n2. The left side is zero, a contradiction. Therefore {κ}≠0 in ordinary Bott–Chern cohomology.

Together with n1, this proves every assertion of A. Pseudoeffectivity is not inferred. Artifact: proofs/n3.txt; rerun python build_notes.py.

notes.summary: C is proved using constancy of the least eigenvalue alone. That value is zero and κ is semipositive. The conclusions hold on actual compact invariant quotients, where every invariant Hermitian metric is Gauduchon.
notes.detailedSummary: A negative constant minimum forces pointwise zero determinant at a finite positive boundary, contradicting B’s increasing actual volume. A positive minimum contradicts integral κ^n=0. No other eigenvalue or rank is assumed constant. Constant entire spectrum gives rank 1 through n−1. Quotient conclusions use actual compactness and invariant coefficients, without classifications or lattice existence.
notes.text:
Let r_1(x)≤...≤r_n(x) be the real relative eigenvalues of κ with respect to ω, and assume ONLY r_1(x)=c is constant.

If c<0, put T=−1/c>0. For 0≤t<T, all factors 1+tr_j(x)≥1+tc>0, so η_t=ω+tκ is positive. At T all factors are nonnegative, and the factor arising from r_1 vanishes at EVERY point. Hence η_T is semipositive with η_T^n=0 pointwise, so V(T)=0. But n2 gives V'(t)>0 on [0,T), with V(0)=integral ω^n>0. Continuity of the actual polynomial yields V(T)≥V(0)>0, a contradiction. Thus c≥0 and κ is semipositive.

If c>0, κ is positive everywhere and integral κ^n>0, contradicting n2. Therefore c=0 everywhere. This used no constancy of the other eigenvalues, their multiplicities, or rank. By n3, {κ} is nonzero. The smooth closed semipositive κ is itself a positive-current representative, with canonical correction u=0. By n1 its ordinary Bott–Chern class has nonnegative pairing against EVERY positive Gauduchon test; indeed the pairings are strictly positive since κ is not identically zero.

If the entire sorted spectrum is constant, the number of positive eigenvalues is constant and at most n−1. It is at least one, because otherwise κ=0 would contradict n2’s positive first integral. Thus rank is constant between 1 and n−1. Under the least-only hypothesis, no constant rank or everywhere-positive lower rank is asserted.

Let X=Γ\G be an ACTUAL connected compact quotient carrying invariant complex structure and invariant strictly LCK tensors. On G choose a frame by left translation from the identity. The complex structure, ω and λ have constant coefficients; exterior and type differentiation preserve invariance, so κ also has constant coefficients. The relative endomorphism consequently has constant numerical matrix and entire spectrum. These descended tensors therefore satisfy the preceding conclusion. This uses invariant coefficients on the covering group, without assuming that a right action preserves the quotient tensors.

For ANY invariant Hermitian metric γ on this quotient, partial and barpartial preserve invariant forms. Thus dd^c(γ^{n−1}) is an invariant real top-degree form and equals bγ^n for a real constant b. This equality descends. Stokes and compactness give 0=integral dd^c(γ^{n−1})=b integral γ^n. Since the last integral is positive, b=0 and γ is Gauduchon, independently of whether it is LCK.

No lattice existence, abstract Lie-algebra compactness, or classification is asserted or invoked. Artifact: proofs/n4.txt; rerun python build_notes.py. This proves restricted C, without resolving unrestricted P03.

notes.summary: D is proved on the actual compact scalar Hopf quotient in every n≥2. Its displayed curvature has a negative eigenvalue, but a bounded smooth correction gives a semipositive representative.
notes.detailedSummary: Directly verifies compactness, descent, positivity, the LCK equation, and Lee period 2 log 2. Calculates spectrum (−ε,1,...,1) at e1. The global correction log ρ−log Φ yields the closed semipositive rank n−1 representative dd^c log ρ, so the example has every-test positivity and is no counterexample.
notes.text:
Fix n≥2 and 0<ε<1. On M=C^n\{0}, let D(z)=z/2. Its integer iterates act freely, since D^kz=z with z≠0 forces k=0. They act properly discontinuously: a compact set has radius in [a,b] with a>0, and only finitely many factors 2^{−k} can make that radial interval meet itself. The quotient H_n=M/<D> is therefore a smooth complex manifold. In polar coordinates z=rv, the action is (v,log r)→(v,log r−log 2). Consequently H_n is diffeomorphic to S^{2n−1}×(R/(log 2)Z), proving actual compactness and connectedness in every dimension.

Let ρ=sum |z_j|^2 and Φ=ρ+ε Re(z_1^2). The estimate (1−ε)ρ≤Φ≤(1+ε)ρ proves Φ>0. The added real part is pluriharmonic, so Ω=dd^cΦ=dd^cρ=(i/(2π))sum dz_j∧d conjugate(z_j)>0. Under D both Φ and Ω scale by 1/4; therefore ω=Ω/Φ descends smoothly and positively. Since log Φ(Dz)=log Φ(z)−2 log 2, λ=−d log Φ is deck invariant and descends closed. Closedness of Ω gives dω=λ∧ω.

The path z(t)=2^{−t}z_0, 0≤t≤1, projects to a closed loop. Its Lee integral is −[log Φ(z(1))−log Φ(z(0))]=2 log 2. Hence λ is nonexact and the metric is strictly LCK. Directly λ^c=−d^c log Φ, so κ=dd^c log Φ.

For the Levi quadratic form H_f(v)=sum f_{j bar k}v_j conjugate(v_k), write p(v)=sum Φ_jv_j. Since H_Φ(v)=|v|^2,
 H_log Φ(v)=|v|^2/Φ−|p(v)|^2/Φ^2.
The common factor i/(2π) cancels in relative eigenvalues. Relative to ω this is identity minus a rank-one nonnegative form, with n−1 eigenvalues 1 and the remaining eigenvalue 1−sum |Φ_j|^2/Φ. At e_1=(1,0,...,0), Φ=1+ε and the derivative vector is (1+ε,0,...,0), so this eigenvalue is −ε. This proves the asserted spectrum exactly.

Set u=log ρ−log Φ. Scaling constants cancel, so u descends globally, smoothly, and boundedly, with −log(1+ε)≤u≤−log(1−ε). It is genuinely quasi-plurisubharmonic by n1. Its corrected representative is κ+dd^c u=dd^c log ρ. Cauchy–Schwarz gives
 H_log ρ(v)=|v|^2/ρ−|sum conjugate(z_j)v_j|^2/ρ^2≥0,
with equality precisely for v∈Cz. Thus the corrected form is descended, smooth, closed, semipositive of rank n−1. It is a positive current in the ordinary Bott–Chern class, nonzero by n3, with nonnegative pairing against EVERY positive Gauduchon test by n1. D is therefore no counterexample to P03.

notes.summary: E is proved, with first positive boundary t=1/ε and exact volume V(t)=(1+t)^{n−1}V(0). Degeneracy occurs only on the stated real rays, while boundary total volume remains positive.
notes.detailedSummary: Calculates h∈[−ε,ε], attaining both endpoints, so the least eigenvalue varies. The boundary factor has numerator 2(1−ε)y^2+R. Exactness gives integral hω^n=0 and the exact integrated determinant polynomial. This identifies the missing everywhere-degeneracy premise in an unrestricted extension of C.
notes.text:
Continue with n5’s actual compact quotient and tensors. Write z_1=x+iy and R=sum_{j>1}|z_j|^2. Then Φ=(1+ε)x^2+(1−ε)y^2+R, Φ_1=(1+ε)x−i(1−ε)y, and Φ_j=conjugate(z_j) for j>1. The exceptional relative eigenvalue is therefore
 h=1−[(1+ε)^2x^2+(1−ε)^2y^2+R]/Φ
  =ε[(1−ε)y^2−(1+ε)x^2]/Φ.
The other n−1 eigenvalues are 1. Rearrangement gives
 (h+ε)Φ=ε[2(1−ε)y^2+R]≥0,
 (ε−h)Φ=ε[2(1+ε)x^2+R]≥0.
Thus −ε≤h≤ε, with endpoints attained at e_1 and i e_1 respectively. Since ε<1, h is the least eigenvalue everywhere and is nonconstant.

For t≥0, η_t=ω+tκ has relative factors 1+t, repeated n−1 times, and 1+th. All are positive for 0≤t<1/ε. At t_0=1/ε the exceptional factor vanishes somewhere; for t>1/ε it is negative at e_1. Hence t_0 is exactly the first positive boundary. There
 1+h/ε=[2(1−ε)y^2+R]/Φ.
Because Φ>0 and 1−ε>0, degeneracy is precisely y=0 and R=0: z=(x,0,...,0) with x real nonzero. These are the real z_1 rays and their quotient images. Everywhere else η_{t_0} is positive, so its top power already has positive integral.

An exact volume formula strengthens this observation. Ordinary determinant identities give κ^n=hω^n and η_t^n=(1+t)^{n−1}(1+th)ω^n. By n2, integral κ^n=0, hence integral hω^n=0. Therefore, for all real t as a polynomial identity,
 V(t)=(1+t)^{n−1}V(0), where V(0)=integral ω^n>0.
In particular V(t_0)=(1+1/ε)^{n−1}V(0)>0. The full positivity interval is −1<t<1/ε: for −1<t<0, h≤ε gives 1+th≥1+tε>0, while the repeated factor requires t>−1.

C’s contradiction requires zero determinant at EVERY point at its boundary. Here that premise fails, because degeneracy occurs only on the specified rays. Thus attaining a negative least eigenvalue somewhere does not reproduce C’s proof when the minimum varies. This establishes E’s failed-extension diagnosis; it does not rule out another proof of unrestricted P03. The example itself has a positive representative by n5.

notes.summary: F is proved for every n≥2 and 0<ε<1 on the same actual compact Hopf quotient. Its least eigenvalue is identically zero while the remaining spectrum varies.
notes.detailedSummary: An all-dimensional Levi square decomposition proves Ω_ε≥(1−ε)dd^c s>0. Descent and Lee period establish strictly LCK tensors. Curvature has rank n−1, with spectra (0,1/(1−ε),...) at e1 and (0,1,...) at e2. This proves that C’s hypothesis is strictly weaker than constant entire spectrum; the example remains pseudoeffective.
notes.text:
On n5’s actual compact connected Hopf quotient, fix n≥2 and 0<ε<1. On the cover put s=sum |z_j|^2>0, q=|z_1|^2, f=q^2/s, Ψ=s+εf, and Ω_ε=dd^cΨ. These are smooth away from zero. The functions s,q,f,Ψ all have homogeneity two under real scaling, so D^*Ψ=Ψ/4 and D^*Ω_ε=Ω_ε/4.

For an arbitrary complex tangent vector v, put b=sum conjugate(z_j)v_j and c=conjugate(z_1)v_1. These are the first directional derivatives of s and q, whose Levi forms are |v|^2 and |v_1|^2. For F(q,s)=q^2/s,
 F_q=2q/s, F_s=−q^2/s^2,
 F_qq=2/s, F_qs=−2q/s^2, F_ss=2q^2/s^3.
The complex chain rule gives the all-dimensional identity
 H_f(v)=(2/s)|c−(q/s)b|^2+(2q/s)|v_1|^2−(q/s)^2|v|^2.
The first two terms are nonnegative and 0≤q/s≤1. Thus H_f(v)≥−|v|^2 and H_Ψ(v)≥(1−ε)|v|^2. With the stipulated dd^c factor this proves Ω_ε≥(1−ε)dd^c s>0, at every point and in every dimension.

Therefore ω_ε=Ω_ε/s descends smoothly and positively. The closed deck-invariant λ=−d log s descends, and dω_ε=λ∧ω_ε. Along z(t)=2^{−t}z_0 its period is 2 log 2, proving nonexactness and strict LCK. The denominator is s, so κ=−dλ^c=dd^c log s. The Cauchy–Schwarz calculation in n5, with s=ρ, proves that κ is semipositive, with kernel Cz and rank n−1. Relative to positive ω_ε it consequently has exactly one zero eigenvalue and no negative eigenvalues; its least eigenvalue is identically zero.

At e_1=(1,0,...,0), s=q=1 and b=c=v_1. The square term vanishes and H_f(v)=|v_1|^2−sum_{j>1}|v_j|^2. Thus H_Ψ is diagonal with entries (1+ε,1−ε,...,1−ε), while H_log s has entries (0,1,...,1). Since s=1, the relative spectrum is (0,1/(1−ε),...,1/(1−ε)). At e_2=(0,1,0,...,0), q=c=0, so H_f=0 and H_Ψ is identity; H_log s has one zero in direction e_2 and n−1 ones. The spectrum is (0,1,...,1). The points lie on distinct coordinate axes and cannot be identified by a scalar deck transformation. These spectra differ for EVERY ε>0.

This gives, in every allowed dimension, an actual compact example with constant least eigenvalue and genuinely nonconstant remaining spectrum. The curvature itself is a smooth closed semipositive representative, with correction zero. Its ordinary Bott–Chern class is nonzero by n3 and has nonnegative pairing against EVERY positive Gauduchon test by n1. F is therefore no counterexample to P03.
